title: The exotic stellar population of Westerlund 1
caption: The super star cluster Westerlund 1, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Westerlund 1 · constellation Ara · about 12000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb), M. G. Guarcello (INAF-OAPA) and the EWOCS team

recognition.text: Ranked #55 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A dense crowd of bright stars fills this frame, each carrying six large and two small diffraction spikes from the telescope's optics. Their sizes and colours vary with brightness, distance and type, and patches of billowing red gas glow around them. This is Westerlund 1, an open cluster that sits behind a vast interstellar cloud of dust and gas.

It is a super star cluster, holding hundreds of very massive stars packed together. Its population has no match elsewhere in the Milky Way, spanning Wolf-Rayet stars, OB supergiants, yellow hypergiants and luminous blue variables. Some shine with almost a million times the Sun's brilliance. Because such stars live short lives, the cluster must be very young, estimated at between 3.5 and 5 million years old.
Super star clusters are thought to be where most of our galaxy's stars formed long ago. Only a few remain, so Westerlund 1 gives astronomers a rare chance to study that era.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.76 x 3.76 arcminutes) and distance (12000 light years), the frame spans roughly 20 × 13 light-years. Its light set out about 12,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam taken for the EWOCS survey, with the shorter-wavelength filters shown in blue, middle ones in green and the longest in red.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it lets Webb see through the dust cloud that dims this cluster in visible light.

explore: The cluster lies roughly 12 000 light-years away in Ara and was discovered in 1961 by Bengt Westerlund. Astronomers believe it holds between 50 000 and 100 000 times the Sun's mass in a region less than six light-years across. Within 40 million years it may host more than 1 500 supernovae.
alt: A dense cluster of bright stars of varied sizes and colours with eight-pointed diffraction spikes, surrounded by patches of billowing red gas against distant stars and galaxies on black.
